title: Equivariant represented right torsors and their fibre isomorphisms
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $G,H$ be group objects in schemes over $B$, using the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] with base $B$. Let $Y$ be a $B$-scheme and $b:G\times_B Y\to Y$ a specified morphism. A $G$-equivariant represented right $H$-torsor over $(Y,b)$ consists of a represented right $H$-torsor $p:P\to Y$ [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors] and a left $G$-action $a:G\times_B P\to P$ with unit and associativity laws, satisfying $p(a(g,x))=b(g,p(x))$ and $a(g,xh)=a(g,x)h$ on every test $B$-scheme. An equivariant isomorphism between two such torsors is a $B$-scheme isomorphism over $Y$ respecting both actions. For any point $o:B\to Y$, let $P_o=P\times_Y B$ and $Q_o=Q\times_Y B$, with canonical inclusions $i_P,i_Q$. A fibre isomorphism is an actual $B$-scheme isomorphism $f:P_o\simeq Q_o$ preserving the two action graphs: for every test $B$-scheme $T$, $g\in G(T)$, $h\in H(T)$ and $x,x'\in P_o(T)$, $a_P(g,i_P(x))=i_P(x')$ implies $a_Q(g,i_Q(f(x)))=i_Q(f(x'))$, and $i_P(x)h=i_P(x')$ implies $i_Q(f(x))h=i_Q(f(x'))$. At a $G$-fixed point $o$, these conditions are precisely equivariance for the induced left $G$- and right $H$-actions on the fibres. For a field $k$ [def-weil-field], use the standard $\mathbf G_m$ and affine line $L=\mathbf G_a$ of [def-sc-gm-ga]. Define the weight-one scaling morphism $\mathbf G_m\times_k L\to L$ by the coordinate algebra map $k[u]\to k[z,z^{-1}]\otimes_k k[u]$, $u\mapsto z\otimes u$, and the origin by $u\mapsto0$.

source.place: Author-hosted https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf, Section 2, Claims 1 and 3, printed pp.2--3, and Lemma 3.6, proof of (2) implies (1), printed p.6; swap s and t for the weight +1 line.
